title: Work placement

paragraphs.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions eleven to fourteen.
Good morning. I'm Alistair. I'm here for a six-month work placement.

Right. Hello, Alistair. I'm Jane Stewart, the office manager. You'll be reporting to me during your time with the company. Now, as you know, we manufacture engines for industrial products, and this office provides the backup administration, record keeping, salary, office supplies, like buying paper and ink for the printers and so on.
Let me tell you about some of the tasks we do in this section and which ones you'll be involved in.

Every morning, the post is delivered to reception, where it's sorted according to departments. The receptionist will phone you when it's ready, and you'll need to go down to pick up the mail for this office, open it, and give every letter to the relevant person. It will need to be done later this morning, as the post hasn't been collected yet. You'll also need to answer the phone, of course. That will mostly be internal calls and calls from suppliers. When customers phone, they normally want to speak with the sales department, and if they are phoning with any trouble, I'll speak to them. If you happen to answer a call from a customer, you should transfer them.

However, I'd love for you to get to know about how we develop relationships with our customers. So once you've settled in, perhaps the day after tomorrow, I'll forward an email for you to read through when you answer them. That'll show you that we take customer service very seriously.

Now, something I'd like you to get on with straight away is to start inputting information about customers into our database. The person who generally does that, Jonathan, has been off sick for a few weeks, and we've got behind with it. We need to take contact details and any changes in the people we deal with in our customer's company and make sure we've got information about what they manufacture, their sales, et cetera.

Listen and answer questions fifteen to twenty. One thing you'll need to do is help me buy office supplies. The first thing, of course, is to decide if we really need them. You don't want to spend money unnecessarily. And if you aren't sure, you'll need to check with me as your line manager. You can ask me directly or by email, but you'll have to get my permission in writing before you can place any order. Then send it to the finance section with a brief summary of what you want to buy. At the same time, request a purchase number from them. This is essential, and we need to have it on the invoice that the supplier sends out. You don't need authorization from finance, but you can only use one of our approved suppliers. You should always try them. If you want to buy from a company that isn't on the list, you must ask finance for advice. Are you with me?

Good. First off, you'll need to fill in an order form which is available on the Internet. Make sure you put in your own name and contact details. Some people forget to do it, so goods arrive and nobody knows who they're for. So fill your form electronically, both to the supplier and finance. All our approved suppliers will accept e-forms. You may be asked to purchase orders for valuable or fragile goods. And for these items, make sure that you and the supplier have signed a contract covering responsibility in the event that the goods are damaged. And for anything that needs installation by the supplier, you must agree a schedule with them. Finally, when the goods arrive, check that you've been sent exactly what you ordered and that nothing has been damaged in transit. If you're satisfied, sign the delivery note, take a photocopy for yourself, and send the original to finance.
We need to order some stationery and printer cartridges now, so let's go through the procedure together. That is the end of section two.
